text.p: LONDON, Dec 20 - IBCA, the European credit rating agency, has today affirmed the A1+ short-term and AA- long-term ratings of Telefonica de Espana (Telefonica).

This follows the announcement of the acceptance of Telefonica Internacional's (TISA) bid for 35% of the voting shares of the Brazilian telecommunications company, Companhia Riograndese de Telecomunicacoes (CRT) and Telefonica's intention to purchase the government's 23.8% stake in TISA.
TISA led the consortium with RBS, a local Brazilian multimedia company, which offered BRR 681 (USD656 million) for the stake.

The federal government of Rio Grande do Sul will retain at least 50% of the voting shares. TISA is a 70% partner in the consortium, in which its two affiliates CTC in Chile and TASA in Argentina will have an additional 7% and 3% stake, respectively. RBS will contribute the remaining 20% and Citicorp has a small symbolic stake at present.

Negotiations are taking place for Citicorp to increase its shareholding in the consortium. CRT is the only operator in basic and mobile telephony in the Rio Grande region and has a concession on a non-exclusive basis to provide these services until the years 2003 and 2007 respectively.

The region, which borders Argentina and Uruguay, is in a strategic position for the Mercosur free market zone and has strong growth potential. Telephone penetration at eight lines per 100 inhabitants is low in a market of nine million inhabitants, of which approximately 75% are located in urban centres.

The potential market is similar in size to that of Chile. At 55%, CRT benefits from good levels of network digitisation. TISA will participate in the management of CRT and will receive a management fee. With its participation in CRT, TISA has become the first foreign operator to have access to the Brazilian telecommunication market and consolidates TISA's position as the principal international telephone operator in Latin America.

Telefonica has also confirmed its interest to purchase the government's present stake in TISA, which is due to be sold in early January, although this is still awaiting final approval from the government.

According to present forecasts, the price will be in the region of ESP100-110 bln and IBCA's ratings are affirmed on the basis that the final price is within this region. This purchase will be a positive factor for the group as it will enable Telefnica to take full control of its international investments. TISA contributed around 15% of total consolidated turnover at end-September 1996. These investments are not expected to worsen the financial profile of the Telefonica group.
